subproblem.title: Exhaustion of an open convex set by convex inner parallel sets with margins
subproblem.statement: For every n ∈ ℕ and every open convex U ⊆ ℝⁿ (ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) there are sets O_j ⊆ ℝⁿ and reals σ_j (j ∈ ℕ) such that: j ↦ O_j is increasing (Monotone); ⋃_j O_j = U; σ_j → 0; and for every j, O_j is open and convex, σ_j > 0, and the closed ball closedBall(x, σ_j) ⊆ U for every x ∈ O_j.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (U : Set (Rn n)), IsOpen U → Convex ℝ U → ∃ (O : ℕ → Set (Rn n)) (σ : ℕ → ℝ), Monotone O ∧ ⋃ j, O j = U ∧ Tendsto σ atTop (𝓝 0) ∧ ∀ j, IsOpen (O j) ∧ Convex ℝ (O j) ∧ 0 < σ j ∧ ∀ x ∈ O j, closedBall x (σ j) ⊆ U
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: this is step B2 of the parent's complete argument (Section B of the supplied proof of Simon 2.7), corresponding to the printed remark "we may take W = {x ∈ U : dist(x, ∂U) > σ} with σ small". The case U = ℝⁿ, where the distance function is useless, is added so that the statement holds for every open convex U, in particular for n = 0.

1. Put σ_j := 1/(j + 1) for j ∈ ℕ. Then σ_j > 0, σ_j is decreasing in j, and σ_j → 0 (tendsto_one_div_add_atTop_nhds_zero_nat).
2. Case U = ℝⁿ (Set.univ). Take O_j := ℝⁿ for every j. The sequence is constant, hence monotone. Its union is ℝⁿ = U, ℝⁿ is open and convex, and closedBall(x, σ_j) ⊆ ℝⁿ = U trivially. All properties hold.
3. Case U ≠ ℝⁿ. Then Uᶜ is nonempty, and it is closed because U is open. Let d(x) := infDist(x, Uᶜ) = inf{dist(x, p) : p ∈ Uᶜ} (Metric.infDist) and O_j := {x : σ_j < d(x)}.
   (a) Key fact: if dist(x, z) < d(x), then z ∈ U. Otherwise z ∈ Uᶜ, and d(x) ≤ dist(x, z) (infDist_le_dist_of_mem), a contradiction.
   (b) Monotone. If i ≤ j, then σ_j ≤ σ_i, so σ_i < d(x) implies σ_j < d(x). Hence O_i ⊆ O_j.
   (c) Open. d is continuous (continuous_infDist_pt), so O_j = d⁻¹((σ_j, ∞)) is open.
   (d) Margin. Let x ∈ O_j and p ∈ closedBall(x, σ_j). Then dist(x, p) ≤ σ_j < d(x), so p ∈ U by (a).
   (e) Union. If x ∈ O_j, then x ∈ closedBall(x, σ_j) ⊆ U by (d) (σ_j > 0). Conversely, let x ∈ U. Then x ∉ Uᶜ, and since Uᶜ is closed and nonempty, d(x) > 0 (IsClosed.notMem_iff_infDist_pos). Choose j with 1/(j + 1) < d(x) (exists_nat_one_div_lt); then x ∈ O_j. Hence ⋃_j O_j = U.
   (f) Convex. Let x, y ∈ O_j, a, b ≥ 0 with a + b = 1, z := a·x + b·y and s := min(d(x), d(y)) > σ_j. We show s ≤ d(z). Since Uᶜ ≠ ∅, it suffices (Metric.le_infDist) to show s ≤ dist(z, p) for every p ∈ Uᶜ. Suppose dist(z, p) < s for some p ∈ Uᶜ, and put v := p − z, so ‖v‖ < s. Then dist(x, x + v) = ‖v‖ < s ≤ d(x), so x + v ∈ U by (a), and likewise y + v ∈ U. By convexity of U, a·(x + v) + b·(y + v) = z + (a + b)·v = z + v = p lies in U, contradicting p ∈ Uᶜ. Hence σ_j < s ≤ d(z), that is, z ∈ O_j.
   (g) σ_j > 0 and σ_j → 0 by step 1.
   Steps (b)–(g) are exactly the required properties. ∎

Formalization note: every Mathlib fact cited above is in the import closure of the frozen GMT.Ch02.Submission; the whole argument was checked in Lean as a single appended theorem with no added imports.
proof_key_steps: If U = univ, take O_j := univ.

Otherwise Uᶜ is closed and nonempty. Let d = infDist(·, Uᶜ) and O_j := {d > σ_j}. O_j is open (d continuous) and increasing, closedBall(x, σ_j) ⊆ U for x ∈ O_j, and ⋃_j O_j = U because d > 0 exactly on U.
Convexity: if ‖v‖ < min(d(x), d(y)) then x+v, y+v ∈ U, so a(x+v) + b(y+v) = z+v ∈ U. Hence d(ax+by) ≥ min(d(x), d(y)) > σ_j.

audit.reason: The prose and type agree. The univ case correctly avoids infDist to an empty complement. Otherwise the closed nonempty complement gives openness, exhaustion and closed-ball margins; the common-translation argument proves convexity. The explicit radii establish positivity, monotonicity of the sets and convergence. No boundedness or positive-dimension hypothesis is silently used.

subproblem.title: Level-set (Markov) step of Simon 2.7: from an arbitrary constant c to β
subproblem.statement: For every n ∈ ℕ, every measurable U ⊆ ℝⁿ (ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), μ = volume = Lebesgue measure), every u : ℝⁿ → ℝ that is a.e.-measurable for μ restricted to U, and all reals θ, β, c with θ > 0: if ofReal θ·μ(U) ≤ min(μ{x ∈ U : β ≤ u(x)}, μ{x ∈ U : u(x) ≤ β}), the level sets being measured by the outer measure μ and not assumed measurable, then ∫⁻_U ‖u(x) − β‖ₑ dx ≤ ofReal(1 + θ⁻¹)·∫⁻_U ‖u(x) − c‖ₑ dx in [0,∞].
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (U : Set (Rn n)) (u : Rn n → ℝ) (θ β c : ℝ), MeasurableSet U → AEMeasurable u (volume.restrict U) → 0 < θ → ENNReal.ofReal θ * volume U ≤ min (volume {x ∈ U | β ≤ u x}) (volume {x ∈ U | u x ≤ β}) → ∫⁻ x in U, ‖u x - β‖ₑ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (1 + θ⁻¹) * ∫⁻ x in U, ‖u x - c‖ₑ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: this is step B5 of the parent's complete argument (Section B of the supplied proof of Simon 2.7). Section B replaces Simon's constants β(σ) → β by the mean ū, then transfers to β using the level-set hypothesis 2.7(*). The argument of B5 never uses that ū is a mean, so it is stated here for an arbitrary constant c.

Notation. ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), μ = volume (Lebesgue measure), μ_U := μ.restrict U. Put I := ∫⁻_U ‖u − c‖ₑ dμ ∈ [0,∞], a := ‖c − β‖ₑ = ofReal|c − β| ∈ [0,∞) and f(x) := ‖u(x) − c‖ₑ. Because u is a.e.-measurable for μ_U, so is f (AEMeasurable.sub_const, then .enorm). All arithmetic is in [0,∞], so the cases I = ∞ or μ(U) = ∞ need no separate treatment.

1. Triangle inequality. For every x, ‖u(x) − β‖ₑ = ‖(u(x) − c) + (c − β)‖ₑ ≤ f(x) + a (enorm_add_le). By monotonicity of the lintegral, additivity against the measurable constant a (lintegral_add_right with measurable_const) and ∫⁻_U a = a·μ(U) (setLIntegral_const):
   ∫⁻_U ‖u − β‖ₑ ≤ I + a·μ(U).
2. Claim: a·(ofReal θ·μ(U)) ≤ I. By Markov's inequality for the a.e.-measurable f (mul_meas_ge_le_lintegral₀): a·μ_U{x : a ≤ f(x)} ≤ ∫⁻ f dμ_U = I. Since U is measurable, μ_U(S) = μ(S ∩ U) for every set S, measurable or not (Measure.restrict_apply'). Also {x : β ≤ u(x)} ∩ U = {x ∈ U : β ≤ u(x)}, and similarly for {u ≤ β}.
   (a) Case c ≤ β. If β ≤ u(x), then u(x) − c ≥ β − c ≥ 0, so f(x) = |u(x) − c| ≥ β − c = |c − β| = a. Hence {x : β ≤ u(x)} ⊆ {x : a ≤ f(x)}. Measure monotonicity holds for outer measures, so the level set need not be measurable. Using the hypothesis (the min is ≤ its first argument):
       a·ofReal θ·μ(U) ≤ a·μ{x ∈ U : β ≤ u(x)} = a·μ_U{x : β ≤ u(x)} ≤ a·μ_U{x : a ≤ f(x)} ≤ I.
   (b) Case β < c. If u(x) ≤ β, then c − u(x) ≥ c − β > 0, so f(x) ≥ c − β = a. Hence {x : u(x) ≤ β} ⊆ {x : a ≤ f(x)}, and the same chain, now using the second argument of the min, gives a·ofReal θ·μ(U) ≤ I.
3. Since θ > 0, ofReal(θ⁻¹)·ofReal(θ) = ofReal(θ⁻¹θ) = ofReal 1 = 1 (ENNReal.ofReal_mul with θ⁻¹ ≥ 0). Hence a·μ(U) = ofReal(θ⁻¹)·(a·(ofReal θ·μ(U))) ≤ ofReal(θ⁻¹)·I by step 2.
4. From steps 1 and 3, ∫⁻_U ‖u − β‖ₑ ≤ I + ofReal(θ⁻¹)·I = (1 + ofReal(θ⁻¹))·I = ofReal(1 + θ⁻¹)·I. The last equality is ENNReal.ofReal_add (1 ≥ 0, θ⁻¹ ≥ 0) with ofReal 1 = 1. This is the claim. ∎

Formalization note: every Mathlib fact cited above is in the import closure of the frozen GMT.Ch02.Submission; the whole argument was checked in Lean as a single appended theorem with no added imports.
proof_key_steps: Integrate the pointwise triangle inequality ‖u−β‖ₑ ≤ ‖u−c‖ₑ + ‖c−β‖ₑ over U: ∫⁻_U‖u−β‖ₑ ≤ I + ‖c−β‖ₑ·μ(U), where I = ∫⁻_U‖u−c‖ₑ.

Apply Markov (mul_meas_ge_le_lintegral₀) to ‖u−c‖ₑ under μ.restrict U. The level set {β ≤ u} (if c ≤ β) or {u ≤ β} (if β < c) lies inside {‖u−c‖ₑ ≥ ‖c−β‖ₑ}, and restrict_apply' holds for measurable U. Together with the hypothesis this gives ‖c−β‖ₑ·ofReal θ·μ(U) ≤ I.
Multiply by ofReal(θ⁻¹), using ofReal(θ⁻¹)·ofReal θ = 1: ‖c−β‖ₑ·μ(U) ≤ ofReal(θ⁻¹)·I. Conclude with I + ofReal(θ⁻¹)·I = ofReal(1+θ⁻¹)·I.

audit.reason: The prose and exact Lean proposition agree, including restricted a.e. measurability and outer-measure level sets. Markov and restrict_apply' justify both sign cases without measurable level-set assumptions. Multiplication by the finite positive reciprocal of θ is valid even for infinite integrals or measure. The proof is complete and non-circular.

subproblem.title: Mean-oscillation bounds pass to the L¹ limit along an increasing exhaustion
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, μ = volume on ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), U ⊆ ℝⁿ with μ(U) < ∞, u integrable on U, O_j ⊆ ℝⁿ (j ∈ ℕ) measurable sets increasing in j with ⋃_j O_j = U, w_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ integrable on O_j, and K ∈ [0,∞]. Suppose e_j := ∫⁻_{O_j} ‖w_j(x) − u(x)‖ₑ dx → 0, and for every j, ∫⁻_{O_j} ‖w_j(x) − c_j‖ₑ dx ≤ K with c_j := μ(O_j).toReal⁻¹·∫_{O_j} w_j. Then ∫⁻_U ‖u(x) − ū‖ₑ dx ≤ K, where ū := μ(U).toReal⁻¹·∫_U u. All integrals of real functions are Bochner integrals; the others are lintegrals in [0,∞].
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (U : Set (Rn n)) (u : Rn n → ℝ) (O : ℕ → Set (Rn n)) (w : ℕ → Rn n → ℝ) (K : ℝ≥0∞), volume U < ⊤ → IntegrableOn u U volume → (∀ j, MeasurableSet (O j)) → Monotone O → ⋃ j, O j = U → (∀ j, IntegrableOn (w j) (O j) volume) → Tendsto (fun j ↦ ∫⁻ x in O j, ‖w j x - u x‖ₑ) atTop (𝓝 0) → (∀ j, ∫⁻ x in O j, ‖w j x - (volume (O j)).toReal⁻¹ * ∫ y in O j, w j y‖ₑ ≤ K) → ∫⁻ x in U, ‖u x - (volume U).toReal⁻¹ * ∫ y in U, u y‖ₑ ≤ K
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: this is step B4 of the parent's complete argument (Section B of the supplied proof of Simon 2.7), corresponding to the printed "The required inequality now follows by letting σ ↓ 0". The specific mollified functions w_j and inner parallel sets U_{σ_j} of B4 are replaced by the abstract properties B4 actually uses: increasing measurable O_j with union U, e_j → 0 and the uniform bound K. As in B4 only the mean of u enters, and here only the inequality ≤ K is needed.

Notation. μ = volume, ū := μ(U).toReal⁻¹·∫_U u, c_j := μ(O_j).toReal⁻¹·∫_{O_j} w_j, e_j := ∫⁻_{O_j} ‖w_j − u‖ₑ.

1. For every j, O_j ⊆ ⋃_k O_k = U.
2. If μ(U) = 0, the left side is a lintegral over a μ-null set, which is 0 ≤ K (setLIntegral_measure_zero). Assume from now on μ(U) ≠ 0. Since μ(U) < ∞, M_R := μ(U).toReal > 0.
3. Measures. By continuity from below for the increasing sequence O_j (tendsto_measure_iUnion_atTop), μ(O_j) → μ(⋃ O_k) = μ(U). Since μ(U) < ∞, μ(O_j).toReal → M_R (ENNReal.tendsto_toReal).
4. Integrals of u. u is integrable on ⋃_j O_j = U, and the O_j are measurable and increasing, so ∫_{O_j} u → ∫_U u (tendsto_setIntegral_of_monotone).
5. Integrals of w_j. u is integrable on O_j ⊆ U, and w_j is integrable on O_j, so ∫_{O_j} w_j − ∫_{O_j} u = ∫_{O_j} (w_j − u) (integral_sub). Hence ‖∫_{O_j} w_j − ∫_{O_j} u‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻_{O_j} ‖w_j − u‖ₑ = e_j (enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm). Since e_j → 0, ∫_{O_j} w_j − ∫_{O_j} u → 0 (tendsto_zero_iff_enorm_tendsto_zero and a squeeze). With step 4, ∫_{O_j} w_j → ∫_U u.
6. Means. By steps 3 and 5 and M_R ≠ 0, c_j = μ(O_j).toReal⁻¹·∫_{O_j} w_j → M_R⁻¹·∫_U u = ū (Tendsto.inv₀, Tendsto.mul). Hence ‖c_j − ū‖ₑ → 0, and, because μ(U) < ∞, ‖c_j − ū‖ₑ·μ(U) → 0 (ENNReal.Tendsto.mul_const). Put r_j := e_j + ‖c_j − ū‖ₑ·μ(U); then r_j → 0.
7. Bound on each O_j. For every x, u(x) − ū = −(w_j(x) − u(x)) + (w_j(x) − c_j) + (c_j − ū), so ‖u(x) − ū‖ₑ ≤ ‖w_j(x) − u(x)‖ₑ + ‖w_j(x) − c_j‖ₑ + ‖c_j − ū‖ₑ. Integrate over O_j. The first summand is a.e.-measurable on O_j because w_j and u are integrable there, and the last is constant, so (lintegral_add_left', lintegral_add_right, setLIntegral_const):
   ∫⁻_{O_j} ‖u − ū‖ₑ ≤ e_j + ∫⁻_{O_j} ‖w_j − c_j‖ₑ + ‖c_j − ū‖ₑ·μ(O_j) ≤ e_j + K + ‖c_j − ū‖ₑ·μ(U) = K + r_j.
   This uses the hypothesis ∫⁻_{O_j} ‖w_j − c_j‖ₑ ≤ K and μ(O_j) ≤ μ(U).
8. Fix j. For every k ≥ j, O_j ⊆ O_k, so ∫⁻_{O_j} ‖u − ū‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻_{O_k} ‖u − ū‖ₑ ≤ K + r_k (lintegral_mono_set and step 7). Since K + r_k → K + 0 = K as k → ∞, ∫⁻_{O_j} ‖u − ū‖ₑ ≤ K (ge_of_tendsto).
9. The family O_j is increasing, hence directed, with union U. So ∫⁻_U ‖u − ū‖ₑ = sup_j ∫⁻_{O_j} ‖u − ū‖ₑ (setLIntegral_iUnion_of_directed, which needs no measurability or finiteness), and this is ≤ K by step 8. ∎

Formalization note: every Mathlib fact cited above is in the import closure of the frozen GMT.Ch02.Submission; the whole argument was checked in Lean as a single appended theorem with no added imports.
proof_key_steps: μ(O_j) → μ(U) by continuity from below, and ∫_{O_j} u → ∫_U u by tendsto_setIntegral_of_monotone.
|∫_{O_j} w_j − ∫_{O_j} u| ≤ e_j → 0, hence c_j → ū and ‖c_j − ū‖ₑ·μ(U) → 0.
Triangle inequality integrated over O_j: ∫⁻_{O_j}‖u − ū‖ₑ ≤ K + e_j + ‖c_j − ū‖ₑ·μ(U) =: K + r_j, with r_j → 0.
Monotonicity in j gives ∫⁻_{O_j}‖u − ū‖ₑ ≤ K for each j. The supremum over the directed family O_j equals ∫⁻_U‖u − ū‖ₑ (setLIntegral_iUnion_of_directed).

subproblem.title: L¹ Poincaré inequality for C¹ functions on bounded open convex sets, constant 2ⁿ·diam
subproblem.statement: For every n ∈ ℕ, every open, bounded, convex O ⊆ ℝⁿ (ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), μ = volume) and every w : ℝⁿ → ℝ of class C¹ (ContDiff ℝ 1 w): ∫⁻_O ‖w(x) − w̄‖ₑ dx ≤ ofReal(2ⁿ·diam O)·∫⁻_O ‖Dw(x)‖ₑ dx in [0,∞]. Here w̄ := μ(O).toReal⁻¹·∫_O w (Bochner integral), diam = Metric.diam, and Dw = fderiv ℝ w with the operator norm. No positivity of μ(O) is assumed (for O = ∅ the left side is 0).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (O : Set (Rn n)) (w : Rn n → ℝ), IsOpen O → Bornology.IsBounded O → Convex ℝ O → ContDiff ℝ 1 w → ∫⁻ x in O, ‖w x - (volume O).toReal⁻¹ * ∫ y in O, w y‖ₑ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (2 ^ n * Metric.diam O) * ∫⁻ x in O, ‖fderiv ℝ w x‖ₑ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: this is step B1 of the parent's complete argument (Section B of the supplied proof of Simon 2.7). Simon's printed proof invokes it as "the usual Poincaré inequality for smooth functions (see e.g. [GT01])". (For comparison, Acosta–Durán, Proc. AMS 132 (2004) 195–202, prove the sharper constant diam/2 for convex domains; only 2ⁿ·diam is needed here.)

Notation. E := ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), μ := volume, finrank ℝ E = n (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin). Dw := fderiv ℝ w with the operator norm. D := diam O = Metric.diam O, w̄ := μ(O).toReal⁻¹·∫_O w (Bochner), A := ∫⁻_O ‖Dw‖ₑ.

1. Trivial case. If O = ∅, the left side is a lintegral over ∅, which is 0. Assume O ≠ ∅. Then m := μ(O) satisfies 0 < m because O is nonempty and open (IsOpen.measure_pos), and m < ∞ because O is bounded (Bornology.IsBounded.measure_lt_top). Put m_R := m.toReal > 0.
2. Regularity. w is differentiable, and x ↦ Dw(x) is continuous (ContDiff.differentiable and ContDiff.continuous_fderiv, order 1 ≠ 0). So G(z) := ‖Dw(z)‖ₑ is continuous, hence measurable. F := 1_O·G (Set.indicator) is measurable because O is open, and ∫⁻_E F = ∫⁻_O G = A (lintegral_indicator). w is continuous, hence integrable on the compact closure of the bounded set O, so w is integrable on O (ContinuousOn.integrableOn_compact on closure O, then mono_set).
3. Dilation identity. For a ∈ E and s > 0, ∫⁻_E F(a + s·y) dy = ofReal((sⁿ)⁻¹)·∫⁻_E F.
   Proof. The pushforward of μ under y ↦ s·y is ofReal(|(s^n)⁻¹|)·μ (Measure.map_addHaar_smul with finrank = n). Hence ∫⁻ F(a + s·y) dy = ∫⁻ F(a + z) d(map) = ofReal((sⁿ)⁻¹)·∫⁻ F(a + z) dz (lintegral_map, lintegral_smul_measure). Finally ∫⁻ F(a + z) dz = ∫⁻ F by translation invariance (lintegral_add_left_eq_self).
   Consequence. If s ≥ 1/2, then s⁻¹ ≤ 2, so ofReal((sⁿ)⁻¹) = ofReal((s⁻¹)ⁿ) ≤ ofReal(2ⁿ) = 2ⁿ, and therefore ∫⁻_E F(a + s·y) dy ≤ 2ⁿ·A.
4. Segment estimate. Let x, y ∈ O. For t ∈ [0,1], γ(t) := x + t(y − x) = (1 − t)x + ty lies in O by convexity. The map φ(t) := w(γ(t)) has derivative φ'(t) = Dw(γ(t))(y − x) for every t (chain rule, HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt), and φ' is continuous. By the fundamental theorem of calculus (intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt), w(y) − w(x) = ∫_0^1 Dw(γ(t))(y − x) dt = ∫_{(0,1]} Dw(γ(t))(y − x) dt. Hence
   ‖w(x) − w(y)‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻_{(0,1]} ‖Dw(γ(t))(y − x)‖ₑ dt ≤ ∫⁻_{(0,1]} ‖Dw(γ(t))‖ₑ·‖y − x‖ₑ dt ≤ ofReal(D)·∫⁻_{(0,1]} F(x + t(y − x)) dt.
   The first inequality is enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm, and the second is the operator-norm bound. The third uses ‖y − x‖ = dist(y, x) ≤ D (dist_le_diam_of_mem, O bounded) and G(γ(t)) = F(γ(t)) since γ(t) ∈ O for t ∈ (0,1]. The constant comes out by lintegral_const_mul'.
5. Double integral. Φ(x, y, t) := F(x + t(y − x)) is measurable on E × E × ℝ (measurable F composed with a continuous map). Integrate step 4 over y ∈ O and then x ∈ O (setLIntegral_mono' on the measurable set O) and pull out the finite constant ofReal(D) (lintegral_const_mul'). Then exchange the order of integration by Tonelli (lintegral_lintegral_swap): first in (y, t) for fixed x, then in (x, t). The function (x, t) ↦ ∫⁻_O Φ(x, y, t) dy is measurable by Measurable.lintegral_prod_right'. This gives
   ∫⁻_O ∫⁻_O ‖w(x) − w(y)‖ₑ dy dx ≤ ofReal(D)·∫⁻_{(0,1]} J(t) dt,  where J(t) := ∫⁻_O ∫⁻_O Φ(x, y, t) dy dx.
6. Claim: J(t) ≤ 2ⁿ·A·m for every t ∈ (0,1].
   (a) t ≥ 1/2. For every x, Φ(x, y, t) = F((1 − t)x + t·y). Hence ∫⁻_O Φ(x, y, t) dy ≤ ∫⁻_E F((1 − t)x + t·y) dy ≤ 2ⁿ·A by step 3 with a = (1 − t)x and s = t. Integrating this constant bound over x ∈ O gives J(t) ≤ 2ⁿ·A·m (setLIntegral_const).
   (b) t < 1/2. By Tonelli, J(t) = ∫⁻_O ∫⁻_O Φ(x, y, t) dx dy. For every y, Φ(x, y, t) = F(t·y + (1 − t)x). Hence ∫⁻_O Φ dx ≤ ∫⁻_E F(t·y + (1 − t)x) dx ≤ 2ⁿ·A by step 3 with a = t·y and s = 1 − t > 1/2. Integrating over y ∈ O gives J(t) ≤ 2ⁿ·A·m.
   Therefore ∫⁻_{(0,1]} J(t) dt ≤ 2ⁿ·A·m·λ((0,1]) = 2ⁿ·A·m (Real.volume_Ioc), and step 5 gives
   (★) ∫⁻_O ∫⁻_O ‖w(x) − w(y)‖ₑ dy dx ≤ ofReal(D)·2ⁿ·A·m.
7. Mean. For every x, ∫_O w(x) dy = m_R·w(x) (setIntegral_const), so ∫_O (w(x) − w(y)) dy = m_R·w(x) − ∫_O w (integral_sub, using that constants and w are integrable on O). Hence w(x) − w̄ = m_R⁻¹·∫_O (w(x) − w(y)) dy. It follows that ‖w(x) − w̄‖ₑ = ofReal(m_R⁻¹)·‖∫_O (w(x) − w(y)) dy‖ₑ ≤ m⁻¹·∫⁻_O ‖w(x) − w(y)‖ₑ dy, because ofReal(m_R⁻¹) = m⁻¹ for 0 < m < ∞ (ENNReal.ofReal_inv_of_pos, ENNReal.ofReal_toReal) and by enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm.
8. Integrate step 7 over x ∈ O, pull out m⁻¹ ≠ ∞ (lintegral_const_mul') and use (★):
   ∫⁻_O ‖w − w̄‖ₑ ≤ m⁻¹·ofReal(D)·2ⁿ·A·m = ofReal(2ⁿ·D)·A.
   The equality holds because m⁻¹·m = 1 (0 < m < ∞, ENNReal.inv_mul_cancel) and 2ⁿ·ofReal(D) = ofReal(2ⁿ·D) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, ENNReal.ofReal_pow). Since A = ∫⁻_O ‖Dw‖ₑ, this is the claim. ∎

Formalization note: every Mathlib fact cited above is in the import closure of the frozen GMT.Ch02.Submission; the whole argument was checked in Lean as a single appended theorem with no added imports.
proof_key_steps: If O = ∅ the left side is 0. Otherwise 0 < μ(O) < ∞, w is integrable on O, and F := 1_O‖Dw‖ₑ is measurable with ∫⁻F = ∫⁻_O‖Dw‖ₑ.
Dilation identity: ∫⁻ F(a + s·y) dy = ofReal(s^{-n})·∫⁻F for s > 0 (map_addHaar_smul plus translation invariance). This is ≤ 2ⁿ·∫⁻_O‖Dw‖ₑ when s ≥ 1/2.
Segment FTC on γ(t) = x + t(y−x) ∈ O (convexity) for x, y ∈ O: ‖w(x)−w(y)‖ₑ ≤ ofReal(diam O)·∫⁻_{(0,1]} F(x + t(y−x)) dt.
Tonelli over O × O × (0,1], then the dilation bound in y (t ≥ 1/2) or in x (t < 1/2), give ∫⁻_O∫⁻_O‖w(x)−w(y)‖ₑ ≤ ofReal(diam O)·2ⁿ·μ(O)·∫⁻_O‖Dw‖ₑ.
Mean step: ‖w(x) − w̄‖ₑ ≤ μ(O)⁻¹·∫⁻_O‖w(x)−w(y)‖ₑ dy. Integrate over x and cancel μ(O)⁻¹·μ(O) = 1.
